summary: For ages 5–7, help children discover that ocean animals need the same basic things as land animals — food, shelter/safety, and the right conditions (oxygen, which fish take from the water through gills while whales, dolphins and sea turtles come up to breathe air, and a suitable temperature) — met in watery ways, and that different parts of the ocean suit different animals. The row's preferred (proposed) approach lets children actively meet an animal's needs and watch a thriving cue respond, with a side-by-side comparison to a familiar land animal and a habitat-matching moment intended to make 'the right conditions' felt rather than recited. This reflects the row's design preference, not an evidenced ranking of media; the sources are unverified.
misconceptions: 'Ocean animals only need water' — they also need food, shelter, and the right conditions, like all animals.
'Fish don't breathe / don't need oxygen' — they take oxygen from the water through gills.
'Any ocean animal can live anywhere in the ocean' — different parts suit different animals (warm reef vs cold deep).
'Ocean animals' needs are completely different from land animals'' — the needs are the same kinds, just met in the water.
'Shelter isn't important underwater' — many animals need hiding places from predators and rough water.

activities.title: Care for an ocean animal: meet its needs and watch it thrive
steps: Choose a sea creature (e.g. a clownfish or a crab) to look after.
Give it food, offer a hiding place (tuck the clownfish into an anemone, the crab under a rock), and set the water conditions.
Watch a simple thriving/happiness cue brighten as each need is met.
Try a pretend habitat-matching step in the scene: drop a warm-reef fish into the very cold deep sea, watch it flag, then move it back to its warm home and see it perk up.
Compare the ocean animal's needs with a familiar pet or garden animal using a side-by-side needs list (food / shelter / right conditions).
activities.insight: Ocean animals need the same kinds of things as all animals — food, shelter or other ways to stay safe, and the right conditions — but met in the water; and different parts of the ocean suit different animals because conditions differ.

activities.title: Tap-to-reveal reef scene: who is meeting which need?
steps: Explore a reef/sea scene and tap each animal to reveal which need it is meeting (tap the clownfish → 'shelter in the anemone'; tap a feeding fish → 'food from smaller creatures').
Point to an animal that is getting food, one getting shelter, and one in water that suits it.
Say in your own words what each animal needs and how it gets it.
activities.insight: Each basic need is met by a real animal doing a real thing — shelter, food, and the right conditions are all visible in the scene.

activities.title: Which ocean home suits me? Animal-to-habitat matching
steps: Look at several ocean zones (warm shallow reef, open sea, seabed, cold dark deep sea) and a set of animals.
Match each animal to the ocean home where its needs are met.
Explain why a warm-reef animal would not do well in the very cold, dark deep sea.
activities.insight: Different parts of the ocean provide for different animals; an animal must be in a place where its needs (right temperature, shelter, food) are met.

activities.title: Does the sea just hand it over? Talk it through
steps: Respond to a prompt: 'A child says ocean animals don't need anything — the sea gives them everything. Do you agree?'
Name what an ocean animal actually needs to survive.
Pick one animal (e.g. a crab) and say where it gets its food and where it hides — naming one thing it must find for itself.
Compare: does a rabbit need the same kinds of things as a fish? Which does the fish get differently?
activities.insight: Ocean animals must find and meet their needs; the sea does not automatically provide everything, and their needs match a land animal's, just met in the water (including oxygen, which fish take in through gills).

checkQuestion: A child says: 'Ocean animals don't really need anything — the sea just gives them everything, so they're not like land animals that need food and a home.' Do you agree? Tell me what an ocean animal actually needs to survive, and whether that's like or unlike a land animal such as a rabbit.
checkAnswer: Disagree — ocean animals need the SAME basic things as land animals: food to eat, a safe place/shelter, and the right conditions (oxygen in the water, the right temperature). The sea doesn't magically hand them everything; they have to find food and shelter, and different parts of the ocean suit different animals. So an ocean animal's needs are much LIKE a rabbit's — just met in the water.
